blocks.title: Session 1 · Area and Circle Geometry

blocks.title: Predict: decompose figures and compute area accurately
content: Why can the same compound figure be decomposed in more than one valid way?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: decompose figures and compute area accurately
content: Area is additive for nonoverlapping pieces.
Choose rectangles, triangles, and circles that minimize unknown dimensions.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: decompose figures and compute area accurately
content: A 15-by-10 rectangle has a 5-by-4 corner removed. Find the remaining area two ways.
verification: Verify all compound-area arithmetic and units.
steps: An additive decomposition of the same region also totals 130 square units.
The result is less than the 150-square-unit bounding rectangle.

blocks.title: You Try: decompose figures and compute area accurately
content: Find the area of a 12-by-9 rectangle with a 4-by-3 corner removed.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: decompose figures and compute area accurately
content: Label units as square units.
Check that the result is smaller than the bounding rectangle.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify all compound-area arithmetic and units.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: decompose figures and compute area accurately
content: Describe two valid decomposition strategies for a compound region.

blocks.title: Predict: use circle terminology and circumference-area formulas
content: If a radius doubles, by what factor do circumference and area change?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: use circle terminology and circumference-area formulas
content: Circumference: $C=2\pi r$.
Area: $A=\pi r^2$.
A sector is bounded by two radii and an arc; a segment is bounded by a chord and arc.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: use circle terminology and circumference-area formulas
content: Compare radii 3 and 6, then find the annulus area between them.
verification: Verify circle and annulus formulas and results.
steps: Circumference changes from $6\pi$ to $12\pi$, so it doubles.
Area changes from $9\pi$ to $36\pi$, so it quadruples.
The annulus area is $36\pi-9\pi=27\pi$ square units.

blocks.title: You Try: use circle terminology and circumference-area formulas
content: A washer has outer radius 8 and inner radius 5. Find its exact area.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: use circle terminology and circumference-area formulas
content: Use radius, not diameter, in formulas.
Subtract circle areas, not radii, for an annulus.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify circle and annulus formulas and results.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: use circle terminology and circumference-area formulas
content: Explain why circle area scales quadratically while circumference scales linearly.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: apply inscribed-angle, chord, and arc theorems
content: How does an inscribed angle compare with its intercepted arc?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: apply inscribed-angle, chord, and arc theorems
content: An inscribed angle measures half its intercepted arc.
Equal chords intercept equal arcs.
Angles formed by intersecting chords use half the sum of intercepted arcs.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: apply inscribed-angle, chord, and arc theorems
content: Find an inscribed angle intercepting a $110^\circ$ arc and a chord angle intercepting arcs $80^\circ$ and $40^\circ$.
verification: Verify every circle theorem against its diagram.
steps: The vertex location determines which half-arc rule applies.

blocks.title: You Try: apply inscribed-angle, chord, and arc theorems
content: An inscribed angle measures 37°. Find its intercepted arc.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: apply inscribed-angle, chord, and arc theorems
content: Identify the vertex location before choosing a theorem.
Do not confuse central and inscribed angles.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify every circle theorem against its diagram.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: apply inscribed-angle, chord, and arc theorems
content: State the vertex-and-arc information needed before applying a circle-angle theorem.

blocks.title: Session 2 · Radians, Motion, and Solids
content: Track units carefully as angles produce distances, speeds, areas, and volumes.

blocks.title: Predict: convert angle measures and compute arc length and sector area
content: Why must the angle be in radians when using $s=r\theta$?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: convert angle measures and compute arc length and sector area
content: Radians measure arc length per radius.
$s=r\theta$ and $A=\tfrac12r^2\theta$ require radians.
Convert degrees using $\theta_{rad}=\theta_{deg}\pi/180$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: convert angle measures and compute arc length and sector area
content: For $r=12$ and $\theta=120^\circ$, find arc length and sector area.
verification: Verify all degree-radian, arc-length, and sector-area calculations.

blocks.title: You Try: convert angle measures and compute arc length and sector area
content: Find the arc length for radius 9 and central angle 40°.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: convert angle measures and compute arc length and sector area
content: Do not insert degrees directly into radian formulas.
Sector area should be the same fraction of $\pi r^2$ as the angle is of a full rotation.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify all degree-radian, arc-length, and sector-area calculations.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: convert angle measures and compute arc length and sector area
content: Explain the unit check that confirms an arc-length calculation.

blocks.title: Predict: relate angular velocity, linear velocity, and distance
content: Why do points farther from the center move faster even when angular speed is the same?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: relate angular velocity, linear velocity, and distance
content: Angular speed: $\omega=\theta/t$.
Linear speed: $v=r\omega$.
Distance: $d=vt=r\theta$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: relate angular velocity, linear velocity, and distance
content: A paddle tip at radius 4 ft rotates at 3 rad/s. Find speed and distance in 10 s.
verification: Verify angular-linear velocity examples and units.
steps: Radians are dimensionless in the linear-speed conversion.

blocks.title: You Try: relate angular velocity, linear velocity, and distance
content: A wheel of radius 0.35 m turns at 8 rad/s. Find rim speed.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: relate angular velocity, linear velocity, and distance
content: Angular units must be radians for $v=r\omega$.
Distinguish revolutions per minute from radians per second.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify angular-linear velocity examples and units.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: relate angular velocity, linear velocity, and distance
content: Describe how radius affects linear speed at fixed angular speed.

blocks.title: Predict: select volume and surface-area formulas for solids
content: Which dimensions contribute to volume, and which surfaces contribute to surface area?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: select volume and surface-area formulas for solids
content: Volume measures three-dimensional capacity; surface area measures exposed two-dimensional faces.
Cylinder: $V=\pi r^2h$ and $SA=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: select volume and surface-area formulas for solids
content: A 10-unit pipe has outer radius 4 and inner radius 3. Find material volume.
verification: Verify all solid-geometry formulas, dimensions, and units.
steps: Subtract the inner cylinder from the outer cylinder.

blocks.title: You Try: select volume and surface-area formulas for solids
content: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 and height 10, then its total surface area.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: select volume and surface-area formulas for solids
content: Use cubic units for volume and square units for area.
A pipe requires outer volume minus inner volume.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify all solid-geometry formulas, dimensions, and units.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: select volume and surface-area formulas for solids
content: Explain how a diagram determines whether to add, subtract, or omit circular bases.
